rejected.title: Using and subverting conventions
card: Conventions are the expected patterns of a form or genre. A fairy tale often opens with "once upon a time" and ends happily. A news report opens with the most important facts.
Follow
a composer uses a convention as audiences expect. This gives a text a familiar shape and meets what the audience is ready for.
Adapt
a composer keeps a convention but changes it to suit a new purpose, such as a fairy tale set in a modern city.
Subvert
a composer deliberately breaks an expected pattern to surprise the audience or make a point. For example, a fairy tale in which the princess rescues herself and refuses to marry.
rejected.remember: Composers can follow, adapt or subvert conventions, and subverting breaks a pattern on purpose.

a.q: What does it mean to subvert a convention?
opts: To break an expected pattern on purpose for effect
To repeat an expected pattern exactly as audiences know it
To keep a pattern but change its setting to a new time
To leave out a pattern because the composer forgot it
a.why: Subverting means deliberately breaking an expected pattern, to surprise the audience or make a point. Keeping the pattern but changing the setting is adapting, not subverting.
a.clue: Recall the princess who rescues herself. What did that tale do?

b.q: Jess writes a detective story. Midway through, the detective gives up and says the crime will never be solved, though readers expect an answer. What has Jess done?
opts: Subverted a convention by withholding the solution
Followed a convention so the story feels familiar
Adapted a convention by moving it to a new setting
Made a mistake, because conventions cannot be broken
b.why: Readers expect a detective story to solve the crime. Jess breaks that pattern on purpose by withholding the solution, so she subverts the convention, which can surprise readers or make a point. Adapting would keep the pattern while changing something such as the setting.
b.clue: What do readers of detective stories expect to happen?

b.q: Jess writes a detective story. Midway through, the detective gives up and says the crime will never be solved, though readers expect an answer. What has Jess done?
opts: Subverted a convention to make a point about justice
Followed a convention so the story feels familiar
Adapted a convention by moving it to a new setting
Made a mistake, because conventions cannot be broken

b.clue: What do readers of detective stories expect to happen?

b.best: Subverted a convention to make a point about justice
